world.description: a pencil logistics and supply network

world.label: Pencil Supply Network
world.summary: Specialists produce and move pencil materials while shops serve customers whose orders keep arriving.

actions.description: Cut pine timber into logs for the sawmill.
Take logs from a timber cutter and make boards.
Mine graphite for pencil lead making.
Take graphite from the mine and make pencil leads.
Take boards from a sawmill and shape pencil slats.
Take slats and leads from their makers and assemble pencils.
Carry pencils from the assembly shop to the stationery shop.
A school customer can place a pencil order, and a shopkeeper can fill an order with shop pencils.

mechanics.rationale: The timber cutter's stated work is cutting timber into logs.
limits: The woodlot has no represented timber stock, so this action cannot check or consume a timber quantity.
tests: The timber cutter gains one log.
A worker with a different role is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The sawyer consumes a log from the named cutter and produces a board.
limits: One log makes one board; no conversion yield beyond that is represented.
tests: A sawyer with a cutter source holding a log consumes one log and gains one board.
A source without a log is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The graphite mine worker's stated work is mining graphite.
limits: No mine capacity or graphite reserve is represented.
tests: The graphite miner gains one graphite.
A worker with a different role is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The lead works consumes graphite from its named source and makes a lead.
limits: One graphite makes one lead; no conversion yield beyond that is represented.
tests: Lead works with a graphite source holding graphite consumes one graphite and gains one lead.
A source without graphite is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The slat mill consumes a board from its named source and shapes a slat.
limits: One board makes one slat; no conversion yield beyond that is represented.
tests: The slat mill consumes one available board and gains one slat.
A source without a board is refused.

mechanics.rationale: The assembler consumes one slat and one lead from the named makers to assemble a pencil.

checks.label: the slat source shapes wooden slats
the lead source makes graphite leads
the slat source has a slat
the lead source has a lead

limits: Assembly requires one slat and one lead; no other materials are represented.
tests: With both named makers holding the required parts, assembly consumes one of each and produces one pencil.
Assembly is refused if either source lacks its required part.
semantic_bindings: The named slat source supplies a slat.
The named lead source supplies a lead.

mechanics.rationale: The carrier moves pencils from the assembly shop to the stationery shop by subtracting from the source and adding to the destination.

checks.label: the worker carries pencils to shops
the destination stocks and sells pencils
the carrier and both shops are at the same location
the destination is at the carrier's location

limits: One action carries one pencil; no transport capacity or larger batch is represented.
tests: The carrier transfers one pencil between co-located assembly and stationery shops.
A source without a pencil or a destination at another location is refused.
semantic_bindings: Pencils arrive at the stationery destination.

mechanics.rationale: A school places an order and the shop fills one waiting order with one shop pencil; the order counter records outstanding demand.

checks.label: the worker stocks and sells pencils
the customer has a waiting order

limits: One action fills one already-arrived order; placing and filling are not separable in this action.
No money, price, or other customer state is represented.
tests: A shop with a pencil fills one waiting school order and consumes one pencil.
The action is refused if the customer has no waiting order or the shop has no pencil.
semantic_bindings: The customer is a school customer who orders pencils.
Filling an order consumes a shop pencil and removes one waiting order.

processes.rationale: Graphite is a raw material mined at its represented source; replenishing the mine's raw-material stock keeps the supply chain running.
The world description says customer orders keep arriving; add one waiting order to the represented school customer each round.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The graphite mine supplied lead works, while the timber cutter’s logs became boards and then slats. The pencil assembler made pencils, the pencil carrier took them to the stationery shop, and the shop filled school orders, though new orders kept arriving faster than they were filled.

mechanisms.name: Goods made from other goods
mechanisms.explanation: Lead works turned graphite into leads, the slat mill turned boards into slats, and the pencil assembler used leads and slats to make pencils.

mechanisms.name: Goods carried to the next step
mechanisms.explanation: The pencil carrier moved pencils from the assembler to the stationery shop.

mechanisms.name: Demand reached and met
mechanisms.explanation: The stationery shop used its pencils to fill the school customer’s waiting orders.

mechanisms.name: Work held up
mechanisms.missing_reason: No event records work being held up while waiting for needed goods.
